title: Nonreciprocal phonon blockade in spin quadratic optomechanical systems
abstract: We propose a scheme for achieving nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical (QOM) system consisting of two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. Due to the Sagnac-Fizeau effect, pump fields propagating in opposite directions experience distinct effective detunings,thereby leading to asymmetric intracavity intensities. Through the optical spring effect, this intensity imbalance gives rise to direction-dependent shifts in the effective mechanical frequency, providing the core mechanism for nonreciprocal phonon blockade. By judiciously setting parameters, single-phonon resonant excitation leads to conventional phonon blockade for one pump direction, whereas two-phonon resonance facilitates phononinduced tunneling (PIT) for the other. The pronounced nonreciprocity is quantified by a contrast ratio in the phonon second-order correlation function exceeding 55 dB. To elucidate the nonreciprocal statistics, the phonon blockade is further analyzed in terms of interference between the coherent component and squeezed fluctuations. Incorporating thermal phonons, we reveal an extended nonreciprocal thermal effect, where increasing thermal noise degrades antibunching toward Poissonian statistics in one direction, yet reverses the statistics from bunching to antibunching in the opposite direction. Our work provides a pathway toward nonreciprocal phonon devices and directional phonon switches, with potential applications in chiral networks and phononic information processing.
summary: The paper details a method to create nonreciprocal phonon blockade in an optomechanical system by exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau effect in two coupled spinning resonators. This asymmetry causes one direction of light pumping to exhibit conventional phonon blockade, while the opposite direction facilitates phonon-induced tunneling. The work provides a pathway for directional quantum control devices.
main_problem: The paper proposes a scheme to achieve nonreciprocal phonon blockade (PB) using a quadratic optomechanical (QOM) system.
main_result: They demonstrate that the Sagnac-Fizeau effect creates direction-dependent mechanical frequency shifts, leading to conventional PB in one pump direction and facilitating two-phonon resonance/tunneling (PIT) in the opposite direction.
method: The analysis involves deriving an effective Hamiltonian for quantum fluctuations and analyzing the system's dynamics using the Lindblad master equation framework.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a QOM system comprising two spinning Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) resonators coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. The nonreciprocity stems from the Sagnac-Fizeau effect causing asymmetric detunings for counter-propagating pump fields.
key_observables: Phonon second-order correlation function ($g^{(2)}_b(0)$), which quantifies blockade (antibunching) or bunching, and direction-dependent effective mechanical frequencies.
important_parameters: The analysis relies on the resolved supermode regime ($J \gg \omega_m, \kappa$) and is sensitive to parameters governing the Sagnac-Fizeau shift ($\Delta F$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions include operating in the weak optomechanical coupling limit and using an analytical wave-function approximation consistent with master equation simulations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the setup (two spinning WGM resonators coupled to a mechanical oscillator) and shows energy level diagrams detailing PB under single-phonon resonance and PIT under two-phonon resonance.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical system and the mechanism of nonreciprocity via the Sagnac-Fizeau effect. It then analyzes the resulting quantum statistics, quantifying the blockade contrast ratio, and finally extends the analysis to include thermal phonons to study extended nonreciprocal effects.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines several advanced topics: cavity QED (optomechanics), nonlinear quantum optics (blockade), and directional control (nonreciprocity) using a specific physical effect (Sagnac-Fizeau).
